  <div class="yk-prose yk-hero__prose">
    <p>I am a machine learning researcher trained in measurement science. On
    Truveta's Intelligence ML team I work across the model lifecycle on longitudinal
    electronic health records. I <strong>train</strong> clinical foundation models,
    including reinforcement learning that steers generated patient journeys toward
    real ones. I build the <strong>benchmarks and
    evaluations</strong> that test them, and the <strong>pipelines</strong> (MCP
    tools, agent systems, dashboards) that carry them into clinical workflows.</p>
    <p>Measurement science is the unusual part of my background. A Ph.D. in
    <strong>measurement and statistics</strong> (University of Washington) and
    postdoctoral training in Harvard's <strong>CARES Lab</strong> (Causality,
    Applications, and Research in Education and Statistics) gave me tools that
    machine learning rarely borrows: validity theory, latent variable models,
    reliability analysis, and the design of randomized trials. I have applied them
    to very different data, from student essays and psychological surveys to
    electronic health records.</p>
    <p>Across all of it, I ask whether a number means what we think it means,
    whether it is a benchmark score, an LLM grader, or a model-estimated
    patient-reported outcome. I ask it at every stage, not just at the end. Validity
    is not a final step; it is a design constraint.</p>
  </div>
